options.label: D
options.text: force of attraction or repulsion depends upon speed of beams.

questions._flag: Official key kept as printed, but recorded as a disagreement for a human (the same finding the 55/2/1 transcription raised about this identical question). Electron and proton beams travelling the same way constitute ANTIPARALLEL conventional currents, so the MAGNETIC force between them is repulsive - which is the reasoning option (b) rewards. The charges are however OPPOSITE, so the Coulomb force is attractive, and at non-relativistic beam speeds it exceeds the magnetic force by roughly \((c/v)^2\), making the NET force attractive. The item is answerable only if the magnetic interaction is read as the one being asked about.

questions.stem: In a Young's double slit experiment, the separation between the two slits is d and distance of the screen from the slits is 1000 d. If the first minima falls at a distance d from the central maximum, obtain the relation between d and \(\lambda\).
questions._flag: Stem is faithful; this note is about the MARKING SCHEME, for whoever authors the solution later. The scheme (ms/p02, Q19) labels its expression 'Position of 1st minima' and then writes \(x_{1d} = \tfrac{3}{2}\cdot\tfrac{\lambda D}{d}\), reaching \(d = 1500\lambda\). \(\tfrac{3}{2}\cdot\tfrac{\lambda D}{d}\) is the SECOND minimum; the first dark fringe is at \(\tfrac{\lambda D}{2d}\), which with D = 1000 d and x = d gives \(d = 500\lambda\). So the scheme's own label and its own algebra disagree. Nothing is changed here - recorded so the discrepancy is adjudicated rather than inherited.
